concept: LiteLLM local Ollama and OpenAI-compatible backends
summary: 12 source-anchored research claims on LiteLLM local Ollama and OpenAI-compatible backends, grouped by facet. Original confidence and source-owner limits are retained.

facts.text: Native tool support is a model/backend capability. Ollama exposes tools and structured tool_calls; LiteLLM's documentation warns that not every Ollama model supports function calling.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: Use ollama_chat/<model> for Ollama POST /api/chat; LiteLLM recommends that path rather than legacy ollama/<model> for conversational responses.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: At the pinned commit, the Ollama Chat adapter forwards native tools directly and sets finish_reason=tool_calls when structured calls appear, including streamed calls.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: Native Ollama api_base points at the server root, such as http://localhost:11434. OpenAI-compatible calls need the backend's API root, commonly ending in /v1, not a full operation URL.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: vLLM automatic tool selection requires --enable-auto-tool-choice, a compatible --tool-call-parser and a tool-compatible chat template. The --chat-template argument is optional when tokenizer_config.json already supplies a suitable template. The cited Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct quickstart uses llama3_json and examples/tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja; those choices are specific to that example. Enabling an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint alone does not configure these model-specific requirements.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner vLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: For Anthropic clients on a chat-only openai/ backend, opt into the Messages-to-Chat path. For clients sending Responses requests, use_chat_completions_api controls a separate Responses-to-Chat bridge.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: Ollama's OpenAI interface has no standard context-size control. Configure context through a Modelfile alias; native Ollama options such as num_ctx belong to a different API path.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: For native Ollama streaming, accumulate thinking, content, and tool_calls and replay the complete assistant turn with tool results in the next request; processing text alone loses tool state.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner Ollama evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: For a generic OpenAI-compatible Chat target, configure openai/<upstream-model>, its api_base, and an upstream API key or required placeholder; gateway and upstream credentials are separate settings.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: Engineering validation should cover schemas, call/result pairing, parallel calls, streamed argument assembly, and follow-up turns. These are separate protocol obligations, not satisfied by a text-only smoke test.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: The pinned native Ollama Chat adapter removes tool_choice rather than enforcing it. Do not rely on forced named, required, or none behavior through this path without validation.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: Schema-constrained output can produce a parseable tool call without a good task decision. Validate semantic arguments and useful tool selection before treating a backend as research-capable.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner vLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

evidenceQualification.scope: Documentation and pinned-code research; native provider sources do not certify the gateway implementation.
